title: Illinois Marijuana Laws: Limits and Travel
metaDescription: Illinois marijuana laws for residents and visitors: possession limits, the medical program, driving rules, and why nothing should cross the Michigan line.
h1: Illinois Marijuana Laws and Crossing Into Michigan

hero.lead: Adults 21 and older can buy and possess cannabis in both Illinois and Michigan, but each state’s rules stop at its border. Here are the Illinois limits for residents and visitors, the driving rules, and why nothing rides along on I-94, as of October 2026.

summary.heading: Illinois at a glance
items: **Adult use:** legal for adults 21 and older under the Cannabis Regulation and Tax Act.
**Visitor limits:** 30 grams of flower, 500 mg of THC in infused products and 5 grams of concentrate; Illinois residents may have twice that.
**Home grow:** registered medical patients only, up to 5 plants.
**Driving:** a numeric THC limit of 5 nanograms per milliliter of whole blood.
**Crossing into Michigan:** Michigan’s rules apply in Michigan, and cannabis may not cross the state line in either direction.

blocks.heading: Is weed legal in Illinois?
blocks.md:
Yes. Illinois allows adults 21 and older to buy and possess cannabis under its Cannabis Regulation and Tax Act. It also runs a separate medical cannabis program for Illinois residents, with registry cards issued by the Illinois Department of Public Health.

Illinois and Michigan both allow adult use, but they set different limits and different driving rules. And because federal law still lists adult-use marijuana in Schedule I as of October 2026, cannabis may not travel between the two states, even though both allow it.

blocks.heading: Possession limits for residents and visitors
blocks.md:
Visitors 21 and older may possess up to 30 grams of cannabis flower, 500 mg of THC in infused products and 5 grams of concentrate. Illinois residents may have twice that: 60 grams of flower, 1,000 mg of THC in infused products and 10 grams of concentrate. The amounts are cumulative across categories, and they reflect a June 2026 law (Public Act 104-0463) that doubled the earlier limits.

Michigan counts differently. Adults 21 and older may carry up to 2.5 ounces there, with no more than 15 grams of it as concentrate, and may keep up to 10 ounces at home.

blocks.heading: The Illinois medical program
blocks.md:
Illinois’ medical cannabis program is for Illinois residents who meet its requirements, and the Illinois Department of Public Health issues the registry cards. Only registered medical patients may grow cannabis at home in Illinois, up to 5 plants.

Visiting Michigan with an Illinois card? Michigan honors valid, unexpired medical cards from other states at licensed medical provisioning centers, with a photo ID. Michigan’s medical purchase limits then apply, up to 2.5 ounces a day and 10 ounces a month, and those purchases are taxed as medical sales, without Michigan’s 10% excise tax. A visiting card does not make you a Michigan registered patient, though: only Michigan residents can get a Michigan card. Our [medical card guide](/getting-a-medical-card/) explains how Michigan’s program works.

blocks.heading: Using cannabis and driving in Illinois
blocks.md:
Illinois’ official guidance says cannabis cannot be used in a motor vehicle, and possession is prohibited on any federal property in the state.

In a moving vehicle, cannabis must be in a sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container in its original packaging. Any other container is a Class A misdemeanor.

Unlike Michigan, Illinois has a numeric THC driving limit: 5 nanograms per milliliter of whole blood, or 10 in another bodily substance, within 2 hours of driving. Michigan has no number; it bans driving under the influence and has a zero-tolerance law for any amount of a Schedule 1 drug, which includes marijuana. In either state the safe plan is the same: if you have used cannabis, do not drive.

blocks.heading: Driving into Michigan on I-94
blocks.md:
Once you cross into Michigan, Michigan’s rules apply. Adults 21 and older can shop at a licensed store with a valid government-issued photo ID, keep within Michigan’s limits and use cannabis only on private property where the owner allows it. Public use is not allowed, no one may use cannabis while driving, and smoking is not allowed in a vehicle’s passenger area on a public road.

Federal land is its own case on both sides of the line. Possession is prohibited on any federal property in Illinois, and Michigan’s law does not protect anyone on federal land, such as a national park or forest.

The trip home is the part to plan for. Illinois’ own guidance says cannabis should not be transported across state lines. Doing so is a federal offense, and Michigan’s law does not protect it either. As of October 2026, federal law still lists adult-use marijuana in Schedule I, and the April 2026 federal rule that moved state-licensed medical marijuana to Schedule III does not say that anyone may carry cannabis between states. Nothing bought in Michigan should ride back to Illinois, and nothing bought in Illinois should ride into Michigan.

Friendly reminder: Enjoy responsibly in Michigan—don’t travel across state lines with cannabis.

items.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older may buy and possess cannabis in Illinois, and Illinois residents can apply to its medical program.

items.q: How much can a non-resident possess in Illinois?
items.a: Up to 30 grams of flower, 500 mg of THC in infused products and 5 grams of concentrate. Illinois residents may have twice that.

items.q: Can I bring weed from Michigan to Illinois?
items.a: No. Illinois’ own guidance says cannabis should not cross state lines. Doing so is a federal offense, and Michigan’s law does not protect it either.

items.q: Can I use an Illinois ID at a Michigan dispensary?
items.a: Yes—valid government-issued ID works (must be 21+). Michigan stores check a valid driver’s license or government-issued photo ID before every sale.

items.q: Is there a THC limit for driving in Illinois?
items.a: Yes: 5 nanograms per milliliter of whole blood, or 10 in another bodily substance, within 2 hours of driving. Michigan has no numeric limit but bans driving under the influence.

items.q: Can I grow cannabis at home in Illinois?
items.a: Only as a registered medical patient, and then up to 5 plants.

items.q: How should cannabis be carried in a car in Illinois?
items.a: In a sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container in its original packaging. Any other container is a Class A misdemeanor.

items.q: Do Illinois possession limits apply in Michigan?
items.a: No. In Michigan, Michigan’s limits apply: adults 21 and older may carry up to 2.5 ounces, with no more than 15 grams of it as concentrate.

items.q: Can I use my Illinois medical card in Michigan?
items.a: Michigan honors valid, unexpired out-of-state medical cards at licensed medical provisioning centers, with a photo ID. Call the store first to ask whether it serves visiting patients.
